# `silk/json_reflect`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Explicit JSON serialization of visible named aggregate fields.

## When to use
Use [`JsonReflect.write`](#declaration-) for a struct whose visible fields each implement `Serialize`.
Call it directly or from the struct's hand-written `Serialize` witness.

## Details
Fields are written in declaration order. Reflection uses this module's visibility, so private
fields of a type declared elsewhere are omitted. The result is that type's visible projection,
not necessarily its complete state. Writing requires no JSON-owned allocation.

## Gotchas
Generic reflected deserialization is unavailable: public reflection can borrow fields but
cannot construct an arbitrary aggregate from decoded owned fields.

Import as `JsonReflect` with `import silk.json_reflect { JsonReflect }`.

Public declarations: 1.

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write<T>(value: &T, options: &JsonOptions)
    -> () ! JsonError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes one JSON object from visible labeled fields in declaration order.

#### Details
Every visible field must implement `Serialize`. Unsupported aggregate kinds and missing
field witnesses fail during specialization. A Writer failure can leave a partial object.


Profiles: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
